title: Perception: Visual Cliff, Pragnanz, Gestalt Laws, Depth Cues
summary: Visual cliff experiment (Gibson & Walk); pragnanz; Gestalt laws of perception (smallness, closure, similarity, proximity); monocular and binocular depth cues; retinal disparity.
objectives: Distinguish monocular from binocular depth cues.
revision: Gestalt laws: similarity, closure, proximity, good continuation. Depth cues: monocular (interposition, relative size, texture, linear perspective, motion parallax) vs binocular (retinal disparity).
traps: Retinal disparity is binocular (needs two eyes).
Closure = filling in gaps to see complete figures.
confusions: Believing all depth cues need two eyes.

notes.t: Gibson & Walk's visual cliff experiment tested depth perception in infants using a glass-covered drop-off. Infants refused to crawl onto the 'deep' side, suggesting innate depth perception.
Pragnanz (law of simplicity) states that we perceive objects in the simplest, most stable way possible.

r: Incomplete figures are perceived as complete
Continuous lines are perceived as connected

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about Gestalt laws and depth cues (monocular vs binocular).
